name: The Haftan (The Seven)
note: The seven primordial holy beings/angels who manifest with each divine theophany; the central angelic heptad of Yarsan cosmology, attested in the Kalam and Hamzeh'ee.

name: The Haftawane (The Seven Other)
note: A second order of seven holy beings ranked beneath the Haftan in Yarsan angelic hierarchy (Hamzeh'ee).

name: Sultan Sahak
note: Soltan Sohak, the central manifestation of the Divine Essence who instituted the present Yarsan dispensation (c. 14th-15th c. Kurdistan); founder figure (Hamzeh'ee, Mir-Hosseini).

name: Khawandagar
note: The first/primordial manifestation of the Divine Essence (Lord-Creator) in the Yarsan chain of mazhariyya (Hamzeh'ee).

name: Shah Khoshin
note: A manifestation of the Divine Essence in the Yarsan succession, placed between Ali and Sultan Sahak in the chain of theophanies (Hamzeh'ee).

name: Pir Benjamin (Binyamin)
note: Foremost of the Haftan, the pir (spiritual master) figure of the heptad in the Sultan Sahak cycle (Hamzeh'ee). Distinct Yarsan figure, not the Israelite patriarch Benjamin (ENT_ISR_BENJAMIN).

name: Dawud (Yarsan Haftan)
note: One of the Haftan, the dalil (guide) figure of the heptad in the Sultan Sahak cycle (Hamzeh'ee). HOMONYM: distinct from the Islamic prophet Dawud/David (ENT_ISL_DAWUD); renamed for disambiguation.

name: Pir Musi
note: One of the Haftan, associated with the recording/scribe function (keeper of deeds) in Yarsan angelology (Hamzeh'ee).

name: Mostafa Dawan
note: One of the Haftan in the Sultan Sahak cycle (Hamzeh'ee).

name: Ramzbar
note: Female holy figure (Razbar/Ramzbar) associated with the Haftan and the Sultan Sahak cycle; one of the few feminine holy figures in Yarsan tradition (Hamzeh'ee, Mir-Hosseini).

name: Divine Essence (Dhat / Haqq)
note: The hidden Divine Essence (Haqq) whose successive human manifestations structure Yarsan theology (Mir-Hosseini).

name: Mazhariyya (chain of manifestation)
note: The doctrine of successive theophanies/manifestations of the Divine Essence in human form (Khawandagar -> Ali -> Shah Khoshin -> Sultan Sahak) (Hamzeh'ee, Mir-Hosseini).

name: Jam (ritual assembly)
note: The communal ritual assembly (jam/jamkhana) central to Yarsan worship, with the votive offering and music; only its public form is modeled here (Mir-Hosseini).

name: Kalam-e Saranjam
note: The corpus of sacred Gorani-language hymns/discourses (Kalam, esp. Saranjam) transmitting Yarsan cosmology and the manifestations (Hamzeh'ee).
